main_issue: Who gets leave on the two working days around Chinese New Year, given that only two of four staff can be off and A, B and D all want both days while C offers to work in return for Christmas off

A-B.evidence: A asks B whether only the first day is needed (T9) and B confirms (T10). B restates having no childcare alternative (T17). Both still compete for the same day and nothing is settled.

A-C.evidence: C offers to work if given Christmas off, so two of the others can be off (T3, T7). A never responds to C, though A's wish for the days off is compatible with C's offer.

A-D.evidence: A asks D whether only the first day is needed (T11). D says both (T12), and A says they also need both (T16). Both claim the same days and neither yields.

B-C.evidence: C's offer to work (T3, T7) would help B, but B never responds to it. B only restates their own need (T6, T10, T17).

B-D.evidence: B needs the first day (T10) and D needs both days (T12). Each states a need for the same day, and neither addresses the other directly.

C-D.evidence: C offers to work so two of the others can be off (T7). D only restates needing both days (T8, T12) and does not respond.
